author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts health officials announced three additional human cases of West Nile virus on Sept. 25, bringing the state's total for 2026 to 11. The Department of Public Health said one case involved a man in his 60s exposed in Suffolk County, another involved a person of unknown age likely exposed in Suffolk County, and the third involved a man in his 90s exposed in Middlesex County.

DPH continues to list Boston, Brookline, Cambridge, Chelsea, Everett, Malden, Newton, Revere, Somerville, Watertown and Winthrop at high risk for West Nile virus. Most of the rest of Massachusetts remains at moderate risk, and officials say the risk will continue until the first hard frost.

State health officials recommend using an EPA-registered repellent, wearing long sleeves and pants, repairing window screens and removing standing water around homes. People in higher-risk areas should consider limiting outdoor activity from dusk to dawn, when mosquitoes are most active.
DPH says its arbovirus surveillance information, including updated West Nile risk levels and positive mosquito results, is posted online as the state continues monitoring the season.
dek: Three additional cases bring Massachusetts' 2026 total to 11, with new exposures reported in Suffolk and Middlesex counties.
headline: Massachusetts reports 11 human West Nile cases as season continues
